turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Sit, I will check the numbers before Doctor Mehta calls you. Who has come with you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I am Krishnan. My daughter only. I don't know why she dragged me, I am having a cough, that is all. The bus was so full, we got late.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sister, please, he has been coughing for weeks. At night I can hear him from the other room. I had to bring him.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Alright, arm straight. Blood pressure is 132 over 78. Pulse 86.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature 36.8, oxygen 96 percent, breathing 20 a minute. Weight is 61 kilos. Any chest pain just now?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no chest pain. The cough is there, I don't know what else to say.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Fine. I have put the readings on the chit. Doctor will see you inside.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come, Mr Krishnan, sit comfortably. I am Dr Mehta. Your daughter is welcome to stay. What has been troubling you?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, this cough. After the flu it started, and the cough itself is not going.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Take your time, there is no hurry. How long has the cough been with you?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): About six weeks, I think. Or since Diwali, or just after Diwali. I don't know, doctor, I cannot put a date on it.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is six weeks. Over Diwali he had fever and body ache, like a flu, and the cough stayed after that.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): And that fever and the body ache, have those settled now?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Fever went. Body ache also went. Only the cough is remaining. I was taking Crocin in those days.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tell me how the cough behaves. What makes it worse?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Night time it is more, I wake up two times or three times, daytime also some cough but night is worse. Mostly dry. Morning, sometimes a little white phlegm, not much.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in that phlegm at all?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No blood. I looked, I don't know, nothing red.
[SEG0019] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, he gets breathless also. Our stairs, he stops in the middle. He will not admit it.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): That is not correct. I am not breathless. I climb only, I feel tired, that is all. I don't know, maybe I am slow these days.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am listening to both. Any loss of weight with this?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No weight loss. I am eating properly, she cooks.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Appetite is holding up? And sleep, apart from the cough?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Appetite is okay. Sleep is broken because of the cough. I don't have sweating in the night. No chills now.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Appa, your shirts are hanging on you. You yourself said the blue collar is loose.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, actually, yes, the trousers also, I pulled the belt in and the clothes are loose. Since when, I don't know. I didn't think that was weight loss, I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that matters, and I will not jump to a name. Any recent travel, or anyone close with a long cough or TB?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No travel. Nobody with TB. I am at home only.

[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His cousin Ramesh in Nagpur was ill, we went there last winter or the winter before, I cannot say which year. People were whispering it could be TB, he coughed for months. Appa stayed in that house one week.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. They never told me it is TB. I don't think I had that kind of contact. It was just a visit, Ramesh had some chest problem.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): So you two remember that visit differently, and the year is foggy. I am not calling this TB today. I only want an X-ray to see the lungs.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): What long-standing problems do you already live with? Sugar, pressure, anything else?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Sugar is there, many years. Pressure also. I take tablets. I don't know all the names, doctor.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Diabetes about twelve years, blood pressure for five or six years. Both are still there. No heart attack, and he has never had an operation.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not even a small operation, stitches, anything?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation. Nothing, I don't know, never.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): The tablets you swallow now, say them in your own words. Colour, purpose, whatever you remember.

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Morning I take my sugar tablet, one only, I think it is 500 but I am not sure of the number. A water tablet for the pressure, small white one, in the morning. And a purple inhaler from my old doctor, I use it when the cough is bad, I don't know the name.

[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The sugar tablet is metformin, written as 500 mg morning and night, but he takes the morning one and skips the night one, I have seen the strip. The water tablet, even I cannot remember the brand, it is for BP. The inhaler is purple and the label has peeled off.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't skip on purpose. I take it when I remember. I don't know, doctor, maybe some nights it is missed. I thought the dose was morning only.

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right, so the strip and what you remember are not the same, and we cannot be sure how many metformin you actually swallow. I will not change anything today. And I will not guess a purple inhaler with no name.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): For the flu I took Crocin, 500 mg, two times a day, for the fever. I stopped when the fever went, maybe ten days back. Not taking it now.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): That is paracetamol, and stopping it was fine. Any other tablet, Ayurvedic, or something from a neighbour?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only what I said.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Did you smoke, or do you still?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I used to, long back. I left it. Last winter, or the one before, I cannot say which. No cigarette now. I don't know the exact time, doctor.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He stopped around that Nagpur trip, whenever it was. Before that, four or five a day. Now zero. He doesn't drink.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): And day to day, what do you do, who is at home?

[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Retired. I was a school clerk. I live with my daughter and her husband. I walk to the temple, that is my exercise, not every day. Sometimes I just sit and read the paper, nothing important.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me listen to the chest. A deep breath, please... and once more.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Throat is not angry. There are a few crackles at the right base, no wheeze. Heart sounds are normal, and I see no swelling of the ankles.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it bad, doctor? I don't know, I get worried.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am not going to put a name on it today. A cough after flu can linger, and loose clothes deserve a proper look, that is all. The X-ray has to show us, not my guess.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Hmm, okay.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am ordering a chest X-ray, to be done this week. No antibiotic from me just now.
[SEG0057] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Can we also do blood, and some TB test? I keep thinking of Ramesh.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the X-ray is unclear, or if the cough has not eased in two weeks, then we might add bloods and think about sputum. Nothing else is arranged now.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): The inhaler, doctor, should I continue? I don't know.
[SEG0060] person_4 (DOCTOR): If it used to help, use the purple inhaler as you were, one or two puffs when the cough is bad. Please don't buy any new tablet at the chemist.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): I sip warm water at night. My neighbour said honey also. Is warm water alright?
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): Warm water is fine, and prop yourself up a little at night. If you see blood, or you are truly gasping, or a high fever comes back, come earlier, don't sit on it.
[SEG0063] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will watch him at night. When do we see you again?
[SEG0064] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back with the X-ray in one week. Reception can book it. If the film is not ready, still come, I don't want this left open.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): One week. I don't know if that X-ray shop near the temple is even open on Sunday. Their shutter was down last time.
[SEG0066] person_1 (NURSE): I can book the chest X-ray in our radiology for Thursday morning, and the review with doctor next Wednesday. You want me to?
[SEG0067] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, please book both. Thursday for the film, and the consultation next Wednesday.
[SEG0068] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He had a cough like this once, last winter, or maybe the winter before that. It went away on its own. We never got an X-ray.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't remember that. I don't know, doctor. Maybe a small cold. I cannot say the year.
[SEG0070] person_4 (DOCTOR): We will leave that old episode unclear. Today is these six weeks.
[SEG0071] person_2 (PATIENT): At home the sugar machine sometimes shows 160, sometimes I forget to check. Do you need it?
[SEG0072] person_4 (DOCTOR): Bring whatever home readings you have, next time. I am not changing the sugar tablet today.
[SEG0073] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will note them. And I am glad you told him about the belt, after saying there was no weight loss.
[SEG0074] person_2 (PATIENT): I was not hiding it. I didn't join the two things. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0075] person_4 (DOCTOR): You were right to correct yourself. Anything else on your mind?
[SEG0076] person_2 (PATIENT): Only, the X-ray, it will pain or what? Foolish question, sorry.
[SEG0077] person_1 (NURSE): It doesn't pain. You stand, they say hold your breath, it is over. I will give the slip outside, and the Thursday time.
[SEG0078] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then we meet next Wednesday, with the film if it is ready. Take care till then, both of you.

spec.situation: Cough for six weeks after flu; worse at night; patient says no weight loss, then says clothes are loose; recent travel or TB contact denied by patient but a family member recalls a cousin's illness; doctor orders chest X-ray, avoids naming a cause.
features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Current metformin supported, but generic name came from family, not patient.
Conditional sputum consideration supported, but transcript says 'think about sputum,' not explicit sputum test.
bad.text: sputum test (type=laboratory, status=conditional, requested_by=doctor, indication=if the X-ray is unclear or the cough has not eased in two weeks)

bad.reason: Doctor may think about sputum later; explicit sputum test not stated.
bad.text: Sputum test (action_type=investigation, status=conditional, responsible_person=doctor, time_reference=value: if the X-ray is unclear or the cough has not eased in two weeks)

omissions.text: Weight loss was initially denied by the patient, then corrected: he reported his trousers and shirts are loose and he had to tighten his belt, suggesting possible weight loss.

Possible TB exposure history is recorded wrongly as family history. What was actually said was a possible contact/exposure: the family member recalled cousin Ramesh in Nagpur may have had TB and the patient stayed in that house for one week; the patient disputed that it was confirmed TB/contact.

Metformin dose/adherence details are incomplete: family member said metformin 500 mg was prescribed morning and night, but the patient usually takes the morning dose and misses/skips some night doses; doctor decided not to change it today because the actual intake is uncertain.
No allergies were discussed/documented in the transcript.
Resolved fever and body aches were associated with a flu-like illness over Diwali, and the patient had taken Crocin during that period; fever/body aches had settled by the time of review.
The cough is mostly dry, with only scant white sputum in the morning.
The patient denied current weight loss at first, but this was contradicted by the family member and then revised by the patient; this disagreement was clinically acknowledged by the doctor.
No one close with a long cough or TB was denied by the patient before the disputed Nagpur exposure was raised.
No other tablets, Ayurvedic medicines, or medicines from a neighbour were being taken.
There was no plan to start antibiotics at this visit, and the doctor specifically said he would not change any of the patient's existing medicines today.
If the current unnamed purple inhaler used to help, the doctor advised continuing it as before at 1–2 puffs when the cough is bad.
Return precautions were specified: come earlier if there is blood, true gasping/breathlessness, or recurrence of high fever.
Follow-up timing detail: the doctor wanted review in one week even if the chest X-ray film was not yet ready, so the issue would not be left open.
